newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian budget proposals at a glance.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian budget proposals at a glance.

text.p: Malaysian Deputy Prime minister and Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim presented the 1997 budget to parliament on Friday. Highlights include:

-- Incentives for companies locating in the newly launched multimedia corridor south of Kuala Lumpur, including a 100 percent corporate tax exemption, easier recruitment of expatriates, and tax exemption on multimedia equipment.
-- Tax incentives to promote the Labuan Offshore Financial Centre, including tax exemptions on foreign workers and professional fees and services.
-- Tax rebates for local fund management firms and tax exemptions for closed-end funds.
-- Formation of a national housing company with start-up capital of one billion ringgit to accelerate a programme to build low and medium-cost housing.
-- Abolition of sales tax on paper and paper products, and various kinds of prepared fish.
-- Reimposition of import duties of five to 20 percent on heavy equipment to spur development of local construction machinery industry.
-- Withdrawal of import duty and sales tax exemptions on spares and consumables used in manufacturing in order to curb imports of intermediate goods and increase local production capacity.
-- Promoting "eco-tourism" by offering the investment tax allowance to low and medium cost hotels and recreational areas in this sector.
-- Incentives to promote the use of natural gas vehicles.

-- Abolition or reduction of import duties on a range of items including dental equipment, cosmetics and soaps, photographic plates and film, textile fibres, carpets, steel wire and some electrical equipment
